channel.title: System Design on the Go
channel.description: System design through collaborative engineering conversations. AI-generated audio and dialogue; verify technical claims against the cited sources.
channel.itunes:author: System Design on the Go

item.title: Designing a Global Video Upload and Playback System at Scale
item.description: An in-depth conversation between two engineers collaboratively designing a large-scale video platform that supports millions of creators and billions of views globally with adaptive streaming, secure storage, and cost-effective delivery using cloud infrastructure.

item.title: Designing a Large-Scale Web Crawler for Language Model Training
item.description: Two engineers discuss building an efficient, fault-tolerant web crawler that starts from seed URLs, extracts HTML text for training large language models, and balances coverage, freshness, and resource constraints. They co-design a prioritization and politeness-aware BFS crawler architecture with multi-stage pipeline processing, hybrid storage, and compliance mechanisms.

item.title: Designing a High-Throughput URL Shortening Service
item.description: Two engineers discuss designing a URL shortener meeting high scalability, availability, and performance requirements. They evaluate hashing versus base62 unique ID approaches, storage and caching strategies, failure modes, and security aspects, converging on distributed ID generation and caching for fast redirects.

item.title: Designing a Scalable, Low-Latency, Health-Aware Load Balancer for Heterogeneous Backends
item.description: Two engineers collaboratively design a production HTTP load balancing system. They discuss trade-offs among common load balancing algorithms—including round robin, weighted round robin, least connections, and latency-aware methods—explore how to incorporate health checks and dynamic weighting, analyze failure scenarios, and consider observability and operational simplicity at scale.

item.title: Designing a Distributed API Rate Limiter Across Multiple Gateways
item.description: A peer-to-peer technical design discussion co-creating a robust distributed API rate limiter. The conversation evaluates strong candidate algorithms, their trade-offs, failure modes, observability, and failure handling to balance burst tolerance, fairness, latency, and operational simplicity in a multi-gateway environment with an external Redis backing store.
